algorithm: For each vertex i in the graph (0 to n-1), count the number of triangles that include i
A triangle is formed by three vertices a, b, c such that (a,b), (b,c), and (c,a) are all edges in the graph
For each vertex i, iterate over its neighbors j and k such that j < k and both j and k are neighbors of i
Check if j and k are connected by an edge to form a triangle with i
Count the number of such valid (j,k) pairs for each i
constraints: Edges are distinct pairs with u < v
No self-loops or duplicate edges in input
edge_cases: n=1: graph has one isolated vertex, triangle count is 0
n=2: graph has two isolated vertices, triangle count is 0
Graph with no edges: all vertices have triangle count 0
Complete graph with n nodes: each vertex has (n-1 choose 2) triangles
Graph with duplicate edges: ignored (edges are distinct per contract)
parsed.inputs: n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n
parsed.output: Dictionary mapping each string vertex key to its integer triangle count
parsed.purpose: Compute the number of triangles for each vertex in a simple undirected unweighted graph
